quandoUsar: Sign-up or password change, when people need to see the rules being met as they type.
Custom password policies: rules, labels, minimum length, and texts are all configurable through props.
Flows that react to strength in code, since `onValueChange` delivers the level and the rules met along with the value.
quandoEvitar: Use `password-field` on login, where measuring strength only gets in the way of people who already have a password.
Use `signup-form` when you need the whole sign-up, with field validation and a completion state.

teclado.acao: On the eye button, which comes right after the field in tab order, show or hide the password.

acessibilidade: The meter has `role="meter"` with `aria-valuenow` from 0 to 4 and `aria-valuetext` with the strength word, and each rule carries a visually hidden “, met” or “, not met” for screen readers.
A `role="status"` region reads a summary after each change (“Strength: Good. 3 of 4 requirements met.”), and the field points to the rule list and the error with `aria-describedby`.
The eye button has a fixed name and reports its state with `aria-pressed`; all texts come in English, so translate them with `messages`, including `levels` and `summary`.
movimento: The four segments enter from the left on a no-overshoot spring, in a wave: a pasted password fills left to right and, when cleared, they empty in the opposite direction.
The strength word moves up when it improves and down when it worsens, each rule met draws a checkmark, the remaining count rolls its digits, and a new error shakes the field once.
With “reduce motion” on, the changes become short or instant fades and the field does not shake.
responsivo: On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the field text goes up to 16px, so the phone keyboard does not zoom in on focus.
notasIA: The default rules require 12 characters, uppercase and lowercase letters, a number, and a symbol; change them with `createPasswordRules({ minLength, labels })` or pass your own `rules` with `test` and, for the count, `remaining`.
Below `shortLength` (8) the meter stays on the first step, with “Too short”, even if the other rules pass; the tests run on every keystroke, so keep `test` cheap.
`onValueChange(valor, força)` brings `level` from 0 to 4 and the ids of the rules met, but scoring runs on the device and only guides the person typing, so also validate the policy on the server.

quandoUsar: Sign-up, checkout, or SMS verification that needs the phone number in E.164 (`+5511961234567`).
Multi-country audiences: people pick the country from the list or paste a number with `+` and the country adjusts on its own.
Forms where formatting while typing prevents errors, with the country mask and a ghost of the missing format.
quandoEvitar: Use `input` with `type="tel"` when the audience is from a single country and E.164 does not matter.
For countries outside the built-in table (49) or to check whether the number exists, use a telephony library, because only the digit count is checked here.

teclado.acao: In the number field, opens the country list already searching by dialing code.
On the country button, open the list; inside it, move the highlight while focus stays on the search.
Jump eight countries at a time in the list.
Go to the first or last country, when the search is empty.
Selects the highlighted country and returns focus to the number, with the cursor at the end.
Closes the list without changing the country and returns focus to the country button.

acessibilidade: The country button announces country and code (“Country, Brazil +55”), and the search is a `combobox` with `aria-activedescendant`, so focus stays on the search field while the highlight moves through the list.
A `role="status"` region announces the country change on paste, the number of search results, and “Valid … number” when the number is complete, and the error message has `role="alert"`.
With `hideLabel`, the label disappears from the screen but remains the field name for screen readers.
movimento: The country button and the list are a single surface: width, height, and corners grow on a no-overshoot spring on open and shrink on close.
When the country changes, flag and code roll in the direction of the list (a country further down enters from below), and the highlight slides between rows on its own spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the surface resizes instantly and flag, messages, and the valid indicator only fade.
responsivo: The list opens at the field width, up to 340px, and scrolls inside with a maximum height of 280px, without dragging the page.
The number uses `type="tel"`, `inputMode="tel"`, and `autoComplete="tel"`, so phones show the phone keyboard and autofill works.
desempenho: The country table ships inside the component, without downloading metadata or depending on a library, and each field keeps a `ResizeObserver` to measure the surface.
notasIA: The value goes in and out as E.164; `onValueChange(valor, details)` also brings country, formatted text, `status`, and `valid`, and with `name` a hidden field submits the E.164 in the form.
The default country is `US`: in Brazil pass `defaultCountry="BR"`; `countries` limits the list and `preferredCountries` pins countries at the top, under “Suggested”.
Country names, search, and messages are in English and there is no translation prop; `error` replaces the validation message, which appears after leaving the field.

quandoUsar: Choosing a plan, shipping option, or region where each option needs a visible description and price.
Single selection among a few options that deserve visual weight, such as in a checkout or an onboarding.
When an unavailable option should stay visible with the reason, via `disabledReason`.
quandoEvitar: Use `radio-group` when each option fits a short label and one supporting line.
Use `select` when there are many options or little screen space.
Use `chip-group` when people can check more than one option.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the next card and select it right away, skipping disabled ones and wrapping to the first after the last.
Do the same for the previous card; in right-to-left layouts, ← and → are swapped.
Select the first or last available card.
Select the focused card.
Enters the group at the selected card, or the first available one, and leaves it in a single keystroke.

acessibilidade: The group has `role="radiogroup"` and each card `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`, named by the label and described by the description.
There is no label prop: pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to `RadioCards`, otherwise the group has no name for screen readers.
Disabled options get `aria-disabled` and show `disabledReason` in place of the description, so the reason is also read aloud.
movimento: A single ring slides from card to card on a no-overshoot spring and the indicator dot grows on the new card; the card itself never changes size.
When the group changes size, the ring follows the new layout instantly, without repeating the slide.
With “reduce motion” on, ring and dot change place instantly and the color transitions are turned off.
responsivo: In `layout="grid"` the columns adjust to the width and drop one by one when they would become narrower than `minColumnWidth` (180px by default); in `list` each option takes the full row.
The label does not wrap and is truncated with an ellipsis; put long text in `description`, which wraps normally.
notasIA: Each option accepts `label`, `description`, `meta` (price or lead time), and `icon`; `meta` sits at the end of the row in `list` and below the text in `grid`.
Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`; with `name`, a hidden field carries the value in the form.
Do not forget the `aria-label` on the group; for text-only options, `radio-group` is simpler and uses native radios.

quandoUsar: Single choice among a few options that should all be visible, such as billing plan or delivery frequency.
Forms where each option has an explanation line below its name.
When you want native radio behavior (arrows, Tab, and form submission) with an animated highlight.
quandoEvitar: Use `radio-cards` when each option needs a price, icon, or card appearance.
Use `select` when the list is long or space is tight.
Use `segmented-control` to switch between views of the same screen.

teclado.acao: Select the next option, as in any native radio, and the highlight slides along.
Select the previous option.
Checks the focused option when none is checked.
Enters the group at the checked option and leaves in a single keystroke.

acessibilidade: It is a `fieldset` with `legend` and native radios sharing the same `name`, so role, group name, and navigation come from the browser.
The name and description of each option live inside the `<label>`, and both become part of the radio's accessible name.
movimento: A single highlight travels to the chosen row on a no-overshoot spring, while the new dot grows and the old one shrinks; rows and texts never change size.
On press, the mark sinks quickly and shows a faint preview dot, and the real dot grows on release.
With “reduce motion” on, highlight and dot change instantly and the color and press transitions are turned off.
notasIA: It is always controlled: `value` and `onValueChange` are required and there is no `defaultValue`, so keep the choice in a `useState`.
Named import, `import { RadioGroup } from "@/components/ryan-ui/radio-group/radio-group"`; `label` becomes the `legend` and each option is `{ value, label, description? }`, text only.
Pass `name` inside a native form; without it, the radios use a generated name.

quandoUsar: Filtering a price range or another measure where seeing the distribution helps people choose, such as nightly rates, salaries, or sizes.
Searches with live filtering, where the lit bars show how much of the set falls inside the range.
quandoEvitar: Use `slider` when there is no data to show the distribution or when a single value is enough.
Use `number-field` when people already know the exact limits and prefer to type them.
Use `chip-group` to filter by categories instead of numbers.

teclado.acao: Increase the focused thumb by one `step`.
Decrease the focused thumb; at a limit, it strains against the edge and springs back.
Move the thumb to the next bar edge in that direction, walking the histogram bar by bar.
Move the thumb to its limit: the end of the scale or the other thumb, respecting the minimum distance.
Moves from the minimum thumb to the maximum one.

acessibilidade: Each thumb is its own `role="slider"`, named “{label}, minimum” and “{label}, maximum” (change with `thumbLabels`), with `aria-valuetext` coming from `format`.
The `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` of each thumb follow the other one, so the screen reader hears only the stretch that is still free.
The histogram and the range text are `aria-hidden`; if the number of items in the range matters, show it as text outside the component, as the demo does.
movimento: The thumbs follow the pointer 1:1, never cross, stretch like elastic past the ends, and on release settle on a nearby bar edge carrying the gesture's velocity.
The bars inside the range light up through a clip that cuts exactly at the thumb, in the same frame, and tapping the chart or track takes the nearest thumb there on a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the thumbs go straight to the value, with no elastic or bump at the limits.
responsivo: It fills the container width, and on touch, dragging vertically still scrolls the page (`touch-action: pan-y`).
desempenho: The bars are recounted when the identity of `data`, `min`, `max`, or `bins` changes; memoize the array with `useMemo` to avoid recounting on every render.
Without `min` and `max`, the limits come from `Math.min(...data)` and `Math.max(...data)` on every render; with many values, pass both.
notasIA: `data` holds the raw values (the price of each listing), not the counts; the component distributes the values into `bins` bars, 32 by default.
Pass explicit `min` and `max`, as the demo does: the default minimum includes zero, so prices from 40 to 600 would open the scale at 0.
Use `onValueChange` for the live text and `onValueCommit` to filter or search, because it fires on release or on every key; `snapToBins={false}` turns off snapping to the edges.

quandoUsar: Asking for a quick rating after a purchase, stay, or support interaction.
Showing the average of reviews with half stars, in `readOnly` mode.
Forms with several criteria, each with its own rating and a supporting line in `description`.
quandoEvitar: Use `reactions` to acknowledge a post with one tap, without a rating scale.
Use `slider` when the scale has many points, such as 0 to 100.
Use `radio-group` when each point on the scale needs its own visible text, as in an agreement scale.

teclado.acao: Raise the rating by one step (half a star with `allowHalf`) and move focus along.
Lower it by one step; below the first star, the rating is cleared if `allowClear` is on.
Go to the lowest or the highest rating.
Give that rating directly, up to the value of `max`.
Clear the rating when `allowClear` is on, which is the default.
Choose the focused star.

acessibilidade: The stars form a `radiogroup` tied to the label, with one `role="radio"` button per value (two per star with `allowHalf`) read as “Great, 4 of 5 stars”, and only the current value is in the Tab order.
With `readOnly`, the group becomes `role="img"` with the rating in its name (“… 4.5 out of 5”) and nothing receives focus.
Pointer choices and a cleared rating are announced in an `aria-live` region; the default words (“Poor” to “Excellent”, “Not rated”) are in English, change them with `valueLabels` and `emptyLabel`.
movimento: On choosing, the fill sweeps the stars from left to right and each one gives a little wave-like hop; quick successive choices, such as a held arrow key, make only the chosen star hop.
Hovering shows a preview over the saved rating, which stays as a faint mark, and the value word rolls in the direction of the change.
With “reduce motion” on, fill, hop, and words change instantly.
responsivo: The `sm`, `md`, and `lg` cells measure 28, 36, and 44px; on touch screens prefer `lg`, and a finger can slide across the stars, with the rating taking effect on release.
When width runs short, the value word drops to the line below; it reserves the space of the longest word and pushes nothing when it changes.
notasIA: `onChange` receives the confirmed rating and 0 means cleared; clicking the current rating again also clears it, unless `allowClear={false}`.
For an average of reviews, use `readOnly` with `allowHalf` and a value like 4.5; values are rounded to the step, half star or whole.
The default words only appear with `max={5}` without half stars, and in other cases the text is “4 out of 5”, so for Portuguese pass `valueLabels` or `showValue={false}`.

quandoUsar: Notes, long comments, product descriptions, or release notes that need headings, lists, and links.
Writers already know Markdown: shortcuts like `## `, `- `, `1. ` and `> ` become formatting as they type.
When you need to store the text as Markdown or clean HTML without bringing in an editor library.
quandoEvitar: Use `textarea` for plain text, without formatting.
Use `mention-input` when what matters is mentions of people and channels, not formatting.
Long documents, tables, images, or collaborative editing call for a full editor; this one covers headings, lists, quotes, code, and links.

teclado.acao: Undoes using the editor's own history; Ctrl + Shift + Z or Ctrl + Y redo (⌘ on Mac).
Bold; Ctrl + I makes italic, Ctrl + Shift + X strikethrough, and Ctrl + E inline code.
Opens the link field in the floating toolbar, where Enter applies and Esc returns to formatting.
At the start of a line or after a space, opens the block menu: ↑ and ↓ choose, Enter or Tab insert, and Esc closes.
In a list, increase or decrease the item's indent; in a code block, Tab inserts two spaces, and outside them focus leaves the editor.
With the floating toolbar open, moves focus to it; ← and → move between the buttons and Esc returns to the text.

acessibilidade: The writing area is `role="textbox"` with `aria-multiline`; pass `aria-label` with the field name, because the default is “Editor”.
The toolbar is a `role="toolbar"` with named buttons and `aria-pressed`, and the block menu is a `listbox` tied to the text by `aria-activedescendant`, so focus does not leave the text when choosing.
An `aria-live` region announces undo, redo, applied Markdown shortcuts, inserted blocks, and links; the interface texts are in English and fixed in the code.
movimento: The floating toolbar appears with a short spring next to the selection, slides when the selection changes, and resizes on a spring when it becomes the link field, with the faces sliding sideways.
In the block menu, a highlight slides between options and the panel follows the height of the filtered results.
With “reduce motion” on, toolbar and menu only fade and change size and position instantly.
responsivo: With the editor under 330px wide (container query), the toolbar hides the block buttons and keeps only the text marks; blocks remain in the slash menu.
Toolbar and menu open upward or downward depending on the visible space in the scrolling or clipping ancestor, so they do not end up hidden.
desempenho: On every change the editor generates HTML, Markdown, and text for the whole document, and undo keeps up to 300 copies of the HTML; it was built for notes and descriptions, not long documents.
notasIA: Start with `defaultMarkdown` or `defaultValue` (HTML) and read `onChange`, which delivers `{ html, markdown, text, empty }`; the controlled `value` only rewrites the content when it differs from the last emitted HTML.
There is no `name` or form field: keep `html` or `markdown` in state; through the `ref` there are `getHTML`, `getMarkdown`, `setMarkdown`, `clear`, `undo`, and `redo`.
Treat `html` as user input and sanitize it on the server before showing it to other people, because the built-in cleanup only covers what is pasted; there is no underline or images.

quandoUsar: Measurements such as height, weight, or temperature, where the tape-measure metaphor helps and the exact value matters.
Touch screens, where dragging and flinging a tape is more comfortable than hitting a small thumb.
Onboarding with one measurement per screen, with the large number and the unit highlighted.
quandoEvitar: Use `slider` when the range is short or when seeing the position on the track matters more than the exact number.
Use `number-field` when people already know the number and prefer to type it.
Use `range-histogram-slider` or a `slider` with two values to choose a range.

teclado.acao: Advance one small mark (`step`), and the tape slides to it on a spring.
Go back one small mark.
Move one labeled mark (`largeStep`, by default `step` times `majorEvery`).
Go to the minimum or the maximum.

acessibilidade: The whole tape is a single focusable `role="slider"`, named by the label, with `aria-valuetext` joining the formatted value and the `unit` (“172 cm”).
The large number and the marks are `aria-hidden`, and the screen reader hears only the slider value, so put the text that should be spoken in `format` and `unit`.
movimento: The tape follows the finger 1:1, keeps sliding with inertia after a fling, and always stops on a mark; pulled past the ends, it stretches like elastic and snaps back.
A tap brings the tapped mark to the needle on a spring, and the digits of the number each roll in their own column while the tape passes.
With “reduce motion” on, the tape goes straight to the value, with no inertia or elastic, and the digits change without rolling.
responsivo: It fills the container width with the tape ends faded; on touch, dragging vertically scrolls the page, and on a trackpad horizontal scrolling moves the tape.
desempenho: The small marks are a CSS background, but each labeled mark is an element and the tape spans the whole range width; for huge ranges with a small `step`, increase `majorEvery` or split the range.
notasIA: Built for physical values with `unit` (cm, kg, °C): `min`, `max`, and `step` define the tape, and `spacing` (px per mark) controls drag precision.
`onValueChange` fires on every mark that passes the needle, including during inertia; save or fetch in `onValueCommit`, which arrives when the tape stops.
The height comes from `--ruler-height` and the width is 100%, so limit the width on the parent element.

quandoUsar: Property panels and inspectors (width, position, rotation, opacity), where dragging is faster than typing.
Numeric fields that benefit from typed calculations and units, such as `320/2 + 8` or `50%`.
Circular values, such as rotation from 0 to 360, with `wrap`.
quandoEvitar: Use `number-field` in ordinary forms, where people expect visible plus and minus buttons.
Use `slider` when the position within the range matters more than the number.
Use `money-input` for monetary values.

teclado.acao: Add or subtract one `step`; with Shift they use `coarseStep` (10× by default) and land on the coarse grid, such as 13 going to 20, and with Alt they use `fineStep` (one tenth).
Confirms the typed text, including calculations such as `(100-24)/2` and units from `units`.
Discards the typed text and returns to the last value; during a label drag, cancels the drag.
Leaving the field confirms the typed text, like Enter.

acessibilidade: The field is a `role="spinbutton"` with `aria-valuetext` that speaks the unit in full (“50 percent”, “45 degrees”) and `aria-invalid` for a moment when a calculation is rejected.
With text in `label`, the `<label>` names the field; with an icon, pass `aria-label`, and the unit button announces itself as “Unit: px. Change unit”.
Dragging the label is pointer-only; by keyboard, the same adjustment is done with the arrow keys and the modifiers.
movimento: At the limits, the field stretches like elastic in the drag direction and springs back on release, and an invalid calculation makes the field shake once.
The fill bar follows the drag 1:1 and slides to typed values; holding Shift or Alt shows a “×10” or “×0.1” tag.
With “reduce motion” on, there is no elastic or shake, the bar jumps to the value, and tags and unit only fade.
responsivo: It fills the whole column (set it with `--scrub-input-width`); on touch, the label drags horizontally and vertical scrolling goes to the page, and pointer lock applies only to mouse.
notasIA: Designed for dense rows: short `label` (“W”, “X”, or a 16px icon with `aria-label`), `min`, `max`, `unit`, and `size="sm"`.
`unit` makes the unit controlled, so handle `onUnitChange`; for the unit button and a typed `50%` to switch the unit on their own, use `defaultUnit`.
`onValueChange` fires on every drag step, with `details.source`; save in `onValueCommit`, which arrives on release, on Enter, on leaving the field, and on each arrow key.

quandoUsar: Filtering a list or table that is already on screen, such as destinations, people, or files.
A search field fixed at the top of a page or sidebar, with a visible label.
quandoEvitar: Use `combobox` when the search ends in choosing an item from the list.
Use `expanding-search` or `morphing-search` when space is tight and the search starts as an icon.
Use `command-palette` to search actions and navigate the whole application by keyboard.

teclado.acao: On the clear button, which enters the tab order after the field when there is text, clear the search and return focus to the field.

acessibilidade: The label is a visible `<label>` tied to the `type="search"` field, and the magnifier is `aria-hidden`.
The clear button has `aria-label="Clear search"`, fixed in English, and returns focus to the field because it disappears from under the pointer.
The component does not announce results: if the list filters live, report the count in your own `aria-live` region.
movimento: The clear button enters with a short spring and a slight blur and leaves quickly; it has a reserved space, so the field never changes width.
The magnifier goes from muted to the text color when the field receives focus or has text.
With “reduce motion” on, the button only fades and the color transitions are turned off.
notasIA: It is always controlled: `value` and `onValueChange(texto)` are required; filter in the parent and, if you call the network, use your own debounce.
Named import, `import { SearchField } from "@/components/ryan-ui/search-field/search-field"`; `label` is required, and the other `<input>` props, such as `placeholder`, pass straight through.

quandoUsar: Switching between a few views of the same information, such as Day, Week, Month, and Year, or Chart and Table.
Single-value filters in toolbars, where the active option must stay visible at all times.
quandoEvitar: Use `tabs` when each option shows its own content panel and needs the tab and panel roles.
Use `toggle-group` when the bar is made of icons or allows several options on at the same time.
Use `select` when there are many options or the labels are long.

teclado.acao: Select the next segment and move focus to it, wrapping to the first after the last.
Select the previous one, also wrapping.
Select the first or last segment.
Goes straight to the selected segment; the others stay out of the tab order.

acessibilidade: It is a `role="group"` of buttons with `aria-pressed` and a single Tab stop; pass `label`, which becomes the group's `aria-label`.
The segments are toggle buttons, not tabs: there is no `tabpanel` tied to them, so the content that changes is the page's responsibility.
movimento: A single pill slides to the chosen segment on a no-overshoot spring; the labels never change size or weight, only the color follows.
With “reduce motion” on, the pill changes place instantly and the scroll to the chosen segment is no longer animated.
responsivo: When the segments do not fit, the track scrolls horizontally inside the control, fades only the side that has more content, and scrolls the chosen segment into view.
On screens under 380px wide, the inner spacing of each segment shrinks.
notasIA: Default export and always controlled: `import SegmentedControl from "@/components/ryan-ui/segmented-control/segmented-control"`, with `options`, `value`, and `onValueChange`.
`onOptionIntent` fires when the pointer or focus reaches a segment, before the choice; use it to preload what the segment will show.
`accessory` puts a badge or counter after the label; the arrows already select, so each keyboard step calls `onValueChange`.

quandoUsar: Choosing a value from a medium-sized list in a form, such as time zone, country, or category.
When space is tight and the options do not need to stay visible all the time.
Forms that need full keyboard support and native submission, with Radix `name` and `required`.
quandoEvitar: Use `radio-group` or `segmented-control` when there are few options and showing all of them is worthwhile.
Use `combobox` when the list is long and people prefer to type to filter.
Use `multi-select` when more than one value can be chosen.

teclado.acao: On the button, open the menu with focus on the selected option.
In the menu, move between options, skipping disabled ones.
Go to the first or last option.
Choose the focused option, close the menu, and return focus to the button.
Closes the menu without changing the value.
Typing the start of a label jumps to that option; with the menu closed, it changes the value right away.

acessibilidade: The button is the Radix `combobox`, tied to the visible `<label>` and to the `description` by `aria-describedby`; the real value sits in hidden text for screen readers while the visible copy animates.
With the menu open, focus is trapped in the options and the rest of the page is hidden from assistive technology, and on close focus returns to the button.
movimento: The menu grows from the button edge with a slight offset and scale, and the arrow rotates; the button never scales, so the menu measures the right position.

The displayed value rolls in the direction of the list, with an option further down entering from below and one further up from above, and the checkmark of the selected option appears with a slight blur.
With “reduce motion” on, menu and value only fade and the checkmark appears without animation.
responsivo: The menu follows the button width and has a maximum height of 320px or the space left on screen, with scroll arrows at the ends, and Radix repositions it so it does not leave the screen.
notasIA: Named import `Select`; pass `options` as `{ value, label, disabled? }` and use `value` with `onValueChange` or `defaultValue`.
Do not use `value=""` on an option: the empty value is the state that shows the `placeholder`.
For search inside the list prefer `combobox`, and for multiple choices, `multi-select`; `className` goes to the button, not to the whole field.

quandoUsar: Preferences screens where people redefine the product's keyboard shortcuts.
Apps with many shortcuts that need a searchable reference sheet, via `ShortcutList`.
Showing shortcuts in menus and texts with drawn keys, via `ShortcutKeys` and `ShortcutKbd`.
quandoEvitar: Use `command-palette` when the goal is to run actions from the keyboard, not to configure them.
To only display a fixed shortcut, use `ShortcutKeys` from this same file, without the recorder.
In apps used almost only by touch, keyboard shortcuts get little use and the settings screen can be left out.

teclado.acao: On the field, start recording; the next combination with a modifier becomes the shortcut.
Cancels recording and keeps the previous shortcut.
Clear the shortcut, during recording or outside it.
During recording, stops recording and moves on to the next control.
Held with the `ShortcutList` on screen, light up that key in every row and fade the rows that do not use it.
In the `ShortcutList` search, clears the typed text.

acessibilidade: The field is a button with `aria-pressed` during recording, named by the label plus the spoken shortcut (“Control Shift L”) and described by the message below.
A `role="status"` region narrates each step: recording start, shortcut set, conflict, clearing, and cancellation; the texts are in English and fixed.
`ShortcutKeys` has `role="img"` with the spoken name of the combination, and the restore and clear buttons have their own `aria-label`.
movimento: The keys enter one after another with a short spring and sink one pixel when held, and a dot pulses slowly while recording.
The message line opens its height on a spring measuring the text, and the restore and clear buttons grow in place.
With “reduce motion” on, the keys only fade, the dot stays still, and nothing sinks.
responsivo: `ShortcutList` uses a container query: from 520px wide, the groups go into two columns.
desempenho: With `highlightPressed` on (the default), `ShortcutList` listens to `keydown` and `keyup` on the whole window in the capture phase; turn it off if you do not use the lit rows.
notasIA: Store the value as text (`"mod+shift+k"`), where `mod` is ⌘ on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere; to trigger the action, use `matchesShortcut(evento, atalho, plataforma)` with `usePlatform()`.
Pass the shortcuts already in use in `bindings` to warn about conflicts; on “Use anyway”, `onValueChange` brings `details.replaced` so you can turn off the old shortcut.
`requireModifier` (default) requires ⌘, Ctrl, or ⌥, except on F keys, and `warnReserved` warns about browser shortcuts such as ⌘W and ⌘C.

quandoUsar: Accepting a contract, terms, or a delivery where people sign with a finger, a stylus, or the mouse.
Flows that store the signature as a PNG or SVG cropped to the ink.
Tablets and phones at a counter, reception, or delivery.
quandoEvitar: When confirming is enough, use an acceptance `checkbox` or `hold-to-confirm`; drawing is slow and has no keyboard alternative.
A signature with strong legal validity calls for a certificate and identity verification, and the pad only captures a drawing.

teclado.acao: With the pad focused, undoes the last stroke (⌘ on Mac).
With the pad focused, redo.
With the pad itself focused, clear the signature, which undo brings back.
With the pad focused, stops playback.
In the color and thickness groups, change the option and move focus along, wrapping around.

acessibilidade: The pad is focusable, with `role="img"` and `aria-roledescription="signature pad"`; the name says how many strokes there are, and a hidden description teaches the shortcuts.
A `role="status"` region announces stroke added, undo, clear, playback, and export, and the icon-only buttons have `aria-label` and `title`.
Drawing has no keyboard alternative: in flows with legal value, also offer another way to sign, such as typing the name.
movimento: The stroke thins with speed, or follows pen pressure, and the ends taper like a nib lifting; clearing sweeps a squeegee across the pad, cutting the ink from left to right.
Playback redraws the strokes at the original pace, with limited pauses and long signatures sped up to about three seconds, and an ink dot follows the tip.
With “reduce motion” on, clearing is immediate and the “Sign here” hint and the buttons only fade.
responsivo: The pad keeps the 600 × 260 aspect ratio and the strokes scale with the width; the toolbar wraps into rows when space runs short.
On touch, the pad blocks scrolling (`touch-action: none`) so the finger can draw, so leave an area outside it for the page to scroll.
desempenho: The live stroke is written straight to the SVG on every movement, without a React re-render, and uses the pointer's coalesced events for a smooth line.
notasIA: There is no `value` and the pad always starts empty: keep the strokes from `onChange` and generate the file with `signatureToPng(traços)` or `signatureToSvg(traços)` to send to the server, instead of the download.
The exports are cropped to the ink, with a transparent background and fixed print colors, so they come out legible on white paper even in the dark theme.
`signer` prints the name under the line, `hint` replaces the “Sign here”, and `label` gives the accessible name; the other internal texts are in English.

quandoUsar: Continuous adjustments where relative position matters: volume, brightness, zoom, opacity.
Filter ranges with two limits, such as budget or price, with a minimum distance between the thumbs.
Scales with a few named points, such as Draft, Good, and Great, using `marks` with a label and `step`.
quandoEvitar: Use `number-field` when the exact value matters and people prefer to type.
Use `range-histogram-slider` when seeing the data distribution helps choose the range.
Use `ruler-slider` for precise measurements with a unit, such as height or weight, on touch screens.

teclado.acao: Increase by one `step`.
Decrease by one `step`; at a limit, the thumb strains against the edge and springs back.
Move by `largeStep`, by default one tenth of the range.
Go to the thumb's limit: the end of the range or, in an interval, the other thumb.
In an interval, moves from one thumb to the other.

acessibilidade: Each thumb is a `role="slider"` with `aria-valuetext` coming from `format`; a single value is named by the label, and in an interval each thumb gets its own name (`thumbLabels` or “…, minimum” and “…, maximum”).
The number beside the label and the bubble are `aria-hidden`, because the slider already speaks the value; icons in `start` and `end` should be `aria-hidden` or named buttons.
movimento: The thumb follows the pointer 1:1, stretches like elastic past the limits, and settles on the `step` grid carrying the gesture's velocity; tapping the track takes the nearest thumb there on a spring.
A bubble with odometer digits follows the thumb while dragging and on keyboard focus, but not on pointer-originated focus, and new digit columns open the width on a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the thumb goes straight to the value, with no elastic or bump, and the digits change without rolling.
responsivo: On touch screens the bubble sits higher, so the finger does not cover it, and never goes past the component edges; dragging vertically still scrolls the page.
notasIA: The value type defines the mode: `defaultValue={60}` gives one thumb, `defaultValue={[800, 2400]}` gives an interval, and `onValueChange` returns the same format.
`onValueChange` fires on every drag step; heavy work, such as filtering or saving, goes in `onValueCommit`, which arrives on release or on each key.
`marks` accepts numbers (tick only) or `{ value, label }` (clickable label), and `start` and `end` take icons, such as low and high volume.

quandoUsar: Preferences that take effect immediately, such as notifications, sync, or features in testing.
Lists of on and off settings, one per row, with the label beside it.
quandoEvitar: Use `checkbox` when the choice only counts after submitting a form or is part of a list of options.
Use `segmented-control` when the two states have names of their own, such as Monthly and Yearly.
Use `theme-switch` to switch between light and dark themes with a page transition.

teclado.acao: Turn on or off; holding Space, the thumb widens as under a finger and travels on release.

acessibilidade: It is the Radix `Switch`: a `<button role="switch">` with `aria-checked`, and inside a `<form>` a hidden field submits `name` and `value`.
The `label` sits inside the button, so clicking the text also toggles, and it becomes the accessible name; without `label`, pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
movimento: The thumb travels on a no-overshoot spring and stops exactly in the state it announces; on press, it widens toward the other side, as under a finger.
Changes without a press, such as via Enter or coming from state, get a short stretch midway, and the track switches to the on color.
With “reduce motion” on, the thumb changes side instantly and the color transitions are turned off.
notasIA: Use it for settings that take effect immediately, without a save button: `checked` with `onCheckedChange` for controlled, or `defaultChecked`.
For text on the left and the switch on the right in a settings row, leave `label` out, write your own text, and link the two with `aria-labelledby`.
It accepts the Radix props (`disabled`, `required`, `name`, `value`); in a form, the value submitted when on is `on`, unless you pass `value`.

quandoUsar: Keywords, topics, or free-form labels typed by the person, such as a post's tags.
Short lists of typed values, such as domains or emails in a filter or invitation.
quandoEvitar: Use `multi-select` when the options come from a known list.
Use `chip-group` for filters with fixed facets that people turn on and off.
Use `mention-input` when the items are mentions of people or channels inside a text.

teclado.acao: Turn the typed text into a tag; leaving the field also adds it, and a duplicate only pulses the one that already exists.
With the cursor at the start of the field, selects the last tag; with one selected, removes it, like Delete.
Move the selection between tags (← from the start of the field); past the last one, return to the text.
Clears the tag selection without removing it.

acessibilidade: Each tag has a “Remove {tag}” button in the tab order, and removing returns focus to the field.
An `aria-live` region announces add, remove, select, and duplicates (“react is already added”); the texts are in English and fixed in the code.
The visible `label` names the field and the `description` is included through `aria-describedby`.
movimento: A new tag appears with a blur where the text was typed while the cursor slides sideways, and on removal the others slide to fill the gap.
The box follows the wrapping rows on a spring, a ring slides between the tags selected by keyboard, and a duplicate pulses.
With “reduce motion” on, the tags only fade, nothing slides, and the box changes height instantly.
responsivo: The tags wrap onto several lines and the box grows with them, with no height limit or inner scrolling.
notasIA: The value is `string[]`, with `value` and `onValueChange` or `defaultValue`; there is no limit on count, no suggestions, and no validation, so filter in `onValueChange` if you need to.
Duplicates are ignored regardless of case, and the comma always separates, so a tag cannot contain a comma.
Named import, `import { TagInput } from "@/components/ryan-ui/tag-input/tag-input"`; the `placeholder` disappears after the first tag.

quandoUsar: Comments, descriptions, order notes, and other multi-line texts without formatting.
Feedback or support fields with an animated help line and validation error.
quandoEvitar: Use `input` for single-line answers, such as a name or subject.
Use `rich-text-editor` when the text needs headings, lists, or links.
Use `prompt-input` for chat or AI message boxes that grow and send with Enter.
acessibilidade: The `label` is a `<label>` tied to the field, and `description` and `error` go into `aria-describedby` together with any `aria-describedby` you pass.
With `error`, the field gets `aria-invalid` and the message has `role="alert"`, so it is read as soon as it appears.
movimento: The help and error messages open their height on a spring and the words rise with a blur; only the words that changed move.
Numbers inside the message, as in “12 characters over the limit”, roll only the digits that changed.
With “reduce motion” on, the messages already appear at their final height and only fade.
notasIA: It accepts the `<textarea>` props (`rows`, `maxLength`, `value`, `onChange`) plus `label`, `description`, and `error`; there is no built-in counter.
The minimum height is 110px, resizable only vertically and not growing with the text; use `rows` for the initial height.
Because it sits in a `role="alert"`, `error` is re-read on every change; avoid an error that changes on every keystroke and show counters outside it.

quandoUsar: Scheduling a meeting, reminder, or delivery with times in fixed steps of 5, 15, or 30 minutes.
Compact forms where a field with a list is faster than typing hours and minutes.
quandoEvitar: Use `wheel-picker` on touch screens, where the wheel gesture is expected, or when some times are unavailable.
Use `date-picker` when the main choice is the day; for day and time, combine the two.
Use `select` when the possible times are few and fixed, such as shifts.

teclado.acao: On the button, open the list centered on the current time; with the list open, choose the highlighted time.
Open the list; when open, move the highlight, wrapping to the start after the end.
Closes the list without changing the time.

acessibilidade: The button has `aria-haspopup="listbox"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls`, and its name joins the label to the chosen time (“Meeting starts 2:30 PM”).
Focus stays on the button while the arrows move the highlight, without `aria-activedescendant`, so the screen reader only hears the new time after the choice.
The list is a `listbox` named “{label} options”, and the chosen option has `aria-selected`.
movimento: The displayed time rolls like a clock: a later time rises from below and an earlier one drops from above.
The list appears with a short spring, a slight offset and scale, already centered on the chosen time, and the arrow rotates.
With “reduce motion” on, the list and the time only fade.
responsivo: The list is as wide as the field and at most 250px tall, scrolling inside without dragging the page.
desempenho: The list renders every time of the day as buttons: 96 with a `minuteStep` of 15, but 1,440 with 1, so prefer steps of 5 or more.
notasIA: The value is always `"HH:MM"` in 24 hours, even with `format="12h"`, which only changes the display to AM and PM.
Use `value` with `onChange` or `defaultValue` (default `"09:00"`); a time outside the `minuteStep` grid is displayed, but does not appear selected in the list.
There is no `name`, minimum time, or blocked times; to block times, use `wheel-picker` with disabled options or validate in the parent.

quandoUsar: Formatting bars where bold, italic, and underline are on at the same time (`type="multiple"`).
Alignment, active tool, or display mode, where only one applies at a time (`single` mode, the default).
Compact icon groups inside editors and panels, with `size="sm"`.
quandoEvitar: Use `segmented-control` to switch between views of a screen, with text labels and a stronger highlight.
Use `button-group` when the buttons trigger actions instead of holding an on or off state.
Use `chip-group` for list filters, with many items that wrap.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the next item, wrapping around, without changing what is pressed.
Move focus to the previous item.
Go to the first or last enabled item.
Press the focused item: in `multiple` they toggle, and in `single` they choose, without deselecting what is already chosen.
Enters the group at the last focused item, or the pressed one, and leaves in a single keystroke.

acessibilidade: In `single` mode the group is a `radiogroup` with `role="radio"` items and `aria-checked`; in `multiple`, it is a `group` of buttons with `aria-pressed`.
The group `label` is required and becomes `aria-label`; for icon-only items, pass `label` on the item, which also becomes the tooltip (`title`).
movimento: In `single`, one fill slides to the chosen option on a no-overshoot spring.
In `multiple`, each fill appears in place and adjacent on items merge into one shape over the gap between them; the icon sinks slightly on press.
With “reduce motion” on, the fill changes place instantly and only color and opacity change, with no scale.
notasIA: Import `ToggleGroup` (default export) and `ToggleGroupItem` from `@/components/ryan-ui/toggle-group/toggle-group`; `type="multiple"` changes the value to `string[]`, and without `type` it is a `string`.
In `single` you cannot deselect by clicking again; if “none” is a valid option, use `multiple` or a dedicated item for it.
The arrows only move focus, even in `single`, unlike a native radio; the choice happens with Space, Enter, or click.

quandoUsar: Choosing a time, duration, or date on touch screens, with the wheel gesture people know from their phones.
Multi-column combinations, such as hour, minute, and AM/PM, or day and shift.
Short lists with unavailable options that need to stay visible, such as fully booked days.
quandoEvitar: Use `time-picker` in desktop forms, where a field with a list takes less space.
Use `select` or `combobox` for long text lists, where reading or typing is faster than spinning.
Use `date-picker` to choose dates on a calendar.

teclado.acao: Spin the focused column by one option, skipping disabled ones.
Spin one screen of options (`visibleCount` minus one).
Go to the first or last enabled option.
Move focus to the previous or next column.
Typing the start of a label jumps to it, as in a native list.

acessibilidade: Each column is a focusable vertical `listbox`, with the column `label` and `aria-activedescendant` pointing to the chosen option; disabled options have `aria-disabled`.
The whole is a `role="group"`: pass `label` on `WheelPicker`, such as “Alarm time”, and a clear `label` on each column, such as “Hour” and “Minute”.
The `suffix` (such as “:” or “min”) is `aria-hidden`; if the unit matters for understanding the column, put it in the column `label`.
movimento: Dragging spins the column with the finger; released with momentum, it keeps going with inertia and stops on the nearest enabled option, with a small elastic give at the ends.
The rows tilt, shrink, and fade as they move away from the center band, as on a drum, and keys and the mouse wheel spin it with a short spring.
With “reduce motion” on, there is no inertia or tilt: the column stops where it was released and the keys jump straight.
responsivo: On touch, the column blocks page scrolling (`touch-action: none`) so the drag spins the wheel; with a mouse, the wheel spins one row per step and, at the ends, lets the page scroll.
desempenho: Each option recalculates tilt and opacity on every frame of the spin, so columns with hundreds of options, such as a list of years, are heavier than hour and minute ones.
notasIA: Describe the columns in `columns` (`id`, `label`, `options`, `suffix`); the value is an object per column, such as `{ hour: "7", minute: "30", period: "AM" }`, and `onValueChange` brings the `columnId` that changed.
Every column always has a value: without a valid value, it takes the first enabled option, and `disabled` options appear struck through and are never where the wheel stops.
`itemHeight` (38px) and `visibleCount` (5, always odd) define the height; each column fits the widest option, or use `width`.
